(!unclustered_indices.empty()) {\n        int max_cardinality = -1;\n        int best_seed = -1;\n        std::vector<int> best_cluster_members;\n        \n        // Try each unclustered point as a seed\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < unclustered_indices.size(); ++i) {\n            const int seed = unclustered_indices[i];\n            if (clustered[seed]) continue;\n            \n best_seed = seed;\n                best_cluster_members = candidate_members;\n            }\n        }\n        \n        // If we found a cluster, add it\n        if (best_seed >= 0 &&      \n            // Mark all members as clustered\n            for (size_t i = 0; i < best_cluster_members.size(); ++i) {\n                clustered[best_cluster_members[i]] = true;\n            }\n Clustering Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Number of points: %d\\n\", num_points);\n    printf(\"Distance threshold: %.2f\\n\", threshold);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : 3.10)\n\nproject(qtclustering)\n\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\n\nadd_executable(qtclustering qtclustering.cpp)\n\ntarget_compile_options(qtclustering PRIVATE -O3 -march=native -Wall -Wextra)\n\n# Link math library\ntarget_link_libraries(qtclustering m)\n// QT Clustering Benchmark - Simplified Sequential Version\n// \n// QT (Quality Threshold) clustering is an algorithm that builds clusters\n// by starting with a seed point and iteratively adding the closest point\n// that maintains the cluster's diameter below a threshold.\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <limits>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nstatic const double MAX_WIDTH = 20.0;\nstatic const double MAX_HEIGHT = 20.0;\n\n// Structure to represent a point in 2D space\nstruct Point {\n    double x, y;\n};\n\n// Structure to represent a cluster\nstruct Cluster {\n    std::vector<int> members;\n    int seed_point;\n};\n\n// Generate synthetic 2D point data in clusters\nvoid generateSyntheticData(std::vector<Point>& points, const int N, unsigned int seed = 42) {\n    auto frand = [&seed]() mutable { return rand_r(&seed) / static_cast<double>(RAND_MAX); };\n    \n    const double min_dim = std::min(MAX_WIDTH, MAX_HEIGHT);\n    int count = 0;\n    \n    while (count < N) {\n        // Create group_cnt points within a circle of radius R\n        // around center point (cntr_x, cntr_y)\n        const double cntr_x = frand() * MAX_WIDTH;\n        const double cntr_y = frand() * MAX_HEIGHT;\n        const double R = frand() * min_dim / 2.0;\n        int group_cnt = static_cast<int>(frand() * (N / 30.0));\n        \n        // Make sure we don't make more points than we need\n        if (group_cnt > (N - count)) {\n            group_cnt = N - count;\n        }\n        \n        while (group_cnt > 0) {\n            const double sign = (frand() < 0.5) ? -1.0 : 1.0;\n            const double r = frand() * R;\n            const double dx = (2.0 * frand() - 1.0) * r;\n            const double dy = std::sqrt(r * r - dx * dx) * sign;\n            const double x = cntr_x + dx;\n            const double y = cntr_y + dy;\n            \n            if (x < 0 || x > MAX_WIDTH || y < 0 || y > MAX_HEIGHT) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            \n            points[count] = {x, y};\n            count++;\n            group_cnt--;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Calculate Euclidean distance between two points\ninline double distance(const Point& p1, const Point& p2) {\n    double dx = p1.x - p2.x;\n    double dy = p1.y - p2.y;\n    return std::sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);\n}\n\n// Find the closest unclustered point to the current cluster that maintains diameter < threshold\n// Returns -1 if no such point exists\nint findClosestPoint(const std::vector<int>& cluster_members,\n                     const std::vector<bool>& clustered,\n                     const std::vector<bool>& in_cluster,\n                     const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                     const double threshold,\n                     const int point_count) {\n    int closest_point = -1;\n    double min_diameter = std::numeric_limits<double>::max();\n    \n    // Try each unclustered point as a candidate\n    for (int candidate = 0; candidate < point_count; ++candidate) {\n        // Skip if already clustered or already in this cluster\n        if (clustered[candidate] || in_cluster[candidate]) continue;\n        \n        // Calculate the maximum distance from candidate to all cluster members\n        double max_dist = 0.0;\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < cluster_members.size(); ++i) {\n            const int member = cluster_members[i];\n            const double dist = distance(points[candidate], points[member]);\n            max_dist = std::max(max_dist, dist);\n        }\n        \n        // If adding this point keeps diameter below threshold and is better than current best\n        if (max_dist < threshold && max_dist < min_diameter) {\n            min_diameter = max_dist;\n            closest_point = candidate;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return closest_point;\n}\n\n// Generate a candidate cluster starting from a seed point\n// Returns the cardinality (size) of the cluster\nint generateCandidateCluster(const int seed_point,\n                              const std::vector<bool>& clustered,\n                              const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                              const double threshold,\n                              const int point_count,\n                              std::vector<int>* cluster_members = nullptr) {\n    std::vector<bool> in_cluster(point_count, false);\n    std::vector<int> members;\n    \n    // Add seed point\n    in_cluster[seed_point] = true;\n    members.push_back(seed_point);\n    \n    // Iteratively add closest points\n    while (static_cast<int>(members.size()) < point_count) {\n        // Find closest point to current cluster that maintains diameter < threshold\n        const int closest = findClosestPoint(members, clustered, in_cluster, points, \n                                             threshold, point_count);\n        \n        if (closest < 0) break; // No more points can be added\n        \n        in_cluster[closest] = true;\n        members.push_back(closest);\n    }\n    \n    // Copy members if requested\n    if (cluster_members) {\n        *cluster_members = members;\n    }\n    \n    return static_cast<int>(members.size());\n}\n\n// Main QT clustering algorithm\nstd::vector<Cluster> qtClustering(const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                                  const double threshold) {\n    const int N = static_cast<int>(points.size());\n    std::vector<bool> clustered(N, false);\n    std::vector<int> unclustered_indices;\n    std::vector<Cluster> clusters;\n    \n    // Initialize unclustered indices\n    for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) {\n        unclustered_indices.push_back(i);\n    }\n    \n    // Main clustering loop\n    while (!unclustered_indices.empty()) {\n        int max_cardinality = -1;\n        int best_seed = -1;\n        std::vector<int> best_cluster_members;\n        \n        // Try each unclustered point as a seed\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < unclustered_indices.size(); ++i) {\n            const int seed = unclustered_indices[i];\n            if (clustered[seed]) continue;\n            \n            std::vector<int> candidate_members;\n            const int cardinality = generateCandidateCluster(seed, clustered, points, \n                                                       threshold, N, \n                                                       &candidate_members);\n            \n            if (cardinality > max_cardinality) {\n                max_cardinality = cardinality;\n                best_seed = seed;\n                best_cluster_members = candidate_members;\n            }\n        }\n        \n        // If we found a cluster, add it\n        if (best_seed >= 0 && max_cardinality > 0) {\n            Cluster cluster;\n            cluster.seed_point = best_seed;\n            cluster.members = best_cluster_members;\n            clusters.push_back(cluster);\n            \n            // Mark all members as clustered\n            for (size_t i = 0; i < best_cluster_members.size(); ++i) {\n                clustered[best_cluster_members[i]] = true;\n            }\n            \n            // Remove clustered points from unclustered list\n            unclustered_indices.erase(\n                std::remove_if(unclustered_indices.begin(), unclustered_indices.end(),\n                              [&clustered](int idx) { return clustered[idx]; }),\n                unclustered_indices.end()\n            );\n        } else {\n            // No more clusters can be formed\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return clusters;\n}\n\n// Validation: check that clusters satisfy the QT clustering properties\nbool validateClusters(const std::vector<Cluster>& clusters,\n                     const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                     const double threshold) {\n    bool valid = true;\n    \n    printf(\"Validating clusters:\\n\");\n    \n    // Check each cluster\n    for (size_t c = 0; c < clusters.size(); ++c) {\n        const auto& cluster = clusters[c];\n        double max_diameter = 0.0;\n        \n        // Check diameter (max distance between any two points)\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < cluster.members.size(); ++i) {\n            for (size_t j = i + 1; j < cluster.members.size(); ++j) {\n                const double dist = distance(points[cluster.members[i]], \n                                           points[cluster.members[j]]);\n                max_diameter = std::max(max_diameter, dist);\n            }\n        }\n        \n        if (c < 10) { // Print first 10 clusters\n            printf(\"  Cluster %zu: size=%zu, seed=%d, diameter=%.4f\\n\", \n                   c, cluster.members.size(), cluster.seed_point, max_diameter);\n        }\n        \n        // Validate diameter is within threshold\n        if (max_diameter > threshold * 1.001) { // Allow small numerical error\n            printf(\"ERROR: Cluster %zu has diameter %.4f > threshold %.4f\\n\", \n                   c, max_diameter, threshold);\n            valid = false;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Check for duplicate memberships\n    std::vector<int> membership(points.size(), -1);\n    for (size_t c = 0; c < clusters.size(); ++c) {\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < clusters[c].members.size(); ++i) {\n            const int member = clusters[c].members[i];\n            if (membership[member] >= 0) {\n                printf(\"ERROR: Point %d appears in multiple clusters (%d and %zu)\\n\",\n                       member, membership[member], c);\n                valid = false;\n            }\n            membership[member] = static_cast<int>(c);\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Count clustered points\n    int clustered_count = 0;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < membership.size(); ++i) {\n        if (membership[i] >= 0) clustered_count++;\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Total points: %zu, Clustered: %d, Unclustered: %zu\\n\",\n           points.size(), clustered_count, points.size() - clustered_count);\n    \n    return valid;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of points (default: 1000)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -t <float>   Distance threshold for clustering (default: 2.0)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    int num_points = 1000;\n    double threshold = 2.0;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            num_points = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-t\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            threshold = atof(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    if (num_points <= 0 || threshold <= 0.0) {\n        printf(\"Error: Invalid parameters (num_points=%d, threshold=%.2f)\\n\", \n               num_points, threshold);\n        return 1;\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"QT Clustering Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Number of points: %d\\n\", num_points);\n    printf(\"Distance threshold: %.2f\\n\", threshold);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    \n    // Generate synthetic data\n    std::vector<Point> points(num_points);\n    generateSyntheticData(points, num_points);\n    \n    // Perform QT clustering\n    auto cluster_start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    \n    const std::vector<Cluster> clusters = qtClustering(points, threshold);\n    \n    auto cluster_end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto cluster_time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(\n        cluster_end - cluster_start);\n    \n    printf(\"Clustering time: %ld ms\\n\", cluster_time.count());\n    printf(\"Clusters found: %zu\\n\", clusters.size());\n    \n    // Calculate statistics and performance metrics\n    int total_clustered = 0;\n    int max_cluster_size = 0;\n    \n    for (size_t i = 0; i < clusters.size(); ++i) {\n        const int size = static_cast<int>(clusters[i].members.size());\n        total_clustered += size;\n        max_cluster_size = std::max(max_cluster_size, size);\n    }\n    \n    const double avg_cluster_size = clusters.empty() ? 0.0 : \n        static_cast<double>(total_clustered) / clusters.size();\n    \n    printf(\"Points clustered: %d / %d (%.1f%%)\\n\", \n           total_clustered, num_points, \n           100.0 * total_clustered / num_points);\n    printf(\"Average cluster size: %.2f\\n\", avg_cluster_size);\n    printf(\"Maximum cluster size: %d\\n\", max_cluster_size);\n    \n    // Performance metrics\n    const double time_sec = cluster_time.count() / 1000.0;\n    const double clusters_per_sec = clusters.size() / time_sec;\n    const double points_per_sec = num_points / time_sec;\n    printf(\"Performance: %.1f clusters/s, %.1f points/s\\n\", \n           clusters_per_sec, points_per_sec);\n    \n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        // Serialize cluster membership for hashing\n        std::vector<double> membershipData;\n        membershipData.reserve(num_points);\n        std::vector<int> membership(num_points, -1);\n        for (size_t c = 0; c < clusters.size(); ++c) {\n            for (size_t i = 0; i < clusters[c].members.size(); ++i) {\n                membership[clusters[c].members[i]] = static_cast<int>(c);\n            }\n        }\n        for (int m : membership) {\n            membershipData.push_back(static_cast<double>(m));\n        }\n        print_results(membershipData, \"ClusterMembership\");\n    }\n    \n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        const bool valid = validateClusters(clusters, points, threshold);\n        \n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n {"type":"step_start","timestamp":1793022050285,"sessionID":"ses_e878ee6f8ffeQv4kFbLWpQ48Ca","part":{"id":"prt_178713fe4001aFCDR6eCwdJQG2","messageID":"msg_178713ad1001Xpsgi12829zq4W","sessionID":"ses_e878ee6f8ffeQv4kFbLWpQ48Ca","type":"step-start"}}
{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793022083585,"sessionID":"ses_e878ee6f8ffeQv4kFbLWpQ48Ca","part":{"id":"prt_178713fe9001Rsa5E8lyvyMuL1","messageID":"msg_178713ad1001Xpsgi12829zq4W","sessionID":"ses_e878ee6f8ffeQv4kFbLWpQ48Ca","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm working through the qtClustering algorithm: for each unclustered seed, grow a candidate cluster greedily, pick the seed yielding the largest cluster, remove its members, and repeat. The hot path is generateCandidateCluster, where findClosestPoint does O(N × members) distance work each iteration as the cluster grows, so I'm thinking about how this cost scales per candidate.\n\nThis gives roughly O(N × C²) per candidate cluster and O(N² × C²) overall, which is expensive — findClosestPoint computes max distance to all current members without early termination, then picks whichever unclustered candidate minimizes that max distance, subject to it being under the threshold (ties go to the first index). I'm also noting edge cases: clustered points are skipped both as seeds and as candidates, the inner loop runs until the cluster reaches point_count, and the outer loop walks unclustered indices in increasing order.\n\nFor parallelizing, I'm thinking of running generateCandidateCluster independently per seed since each only reads shared state and writes to its own output, using something like an OpenMP parallel-for with per-seed results collected into an array. To preserve exact semantics (pick the seed yielding the largest cluster, ties broken by lowest seed index), I'd do the reduction sequentially afterward rather than in parallel. To avoid storing full candidate-member lists for every seed, I'm considering computing just the cardinality per seed in parallel, then finding the first index achieving the max, and recomputing that one seed's cluster membership afterward.\n\nAlternatively, a custom reduction could keep each thread's local best as (cardinality, seed, members), updating only on strict improvement or on a tie with a smaller seed index, then combining threads' bests under a critical section using the same rule—this is equivalent to the sequential first-occurrence-of-max behavior and avoids recomputation while only copying members when a thread's local best actually improves.\n\nI also realize a real algorithmic win is possible without changing outputs: instead of recomputing distance from each candidate to every cluster member at each growth step (O(N·C)), I can maintain a running max distance per candidate that updates incrementally as members are added, since max is exact and order-independent for floating point, reducing cost to O(N) per step while keeping identical results.\n\nI'm weighing whether the incremental max-distance tracking counts as acceptable optimization within \"parallelize while maintaining correctness\" — I decide it's worth doing since it preserves identical output while cutting redundant work, and I'll verify numerically against the original across multiple sizes and thresholds. For each seed I need a per-thread workspace holding a maxd array and an in_cluster array sized to N, avoiding shared-state conflicts across threads.\n\nI'm fusing the closest-candidate scan with the max-distance update into a single pass per step, so for each candidate I compute the new max distance and check it against both the threshold and current best simultaneously, skipping points already clustered or already in the current cluster.\n\nThen I realize a key pruning trick: since maxd is monotone non-decreasing, once a candidate's max distance crosses the threshold it can never be chosen again, so I can permanently drop it from an active list rather than rescanning it every step — this shrinks the working set fast as clusters tighten. I'm working out how to maintain this active list with order-preserving compaction so tie-breaking by smallest index still holds, while picking the minimum maxd among survivors as the next member to add.\n\nSo the algorithm starts with members holding the seed, builds the active set, then iteratively selects the best candidate (smallest max-distance under threshold, ties broken by index), adds it to members, and refreshes the active set's distances against the new member, pruning anything exceeding threshold—continuing until no valid candidate remains.\n\nOrder of members doesn't affect membership or stats, so appending in selection order stays consistent with the original. Then I verify the outer loop over unclustered seeds (ascending index) picks the seed yielding the largest cluster, with ties broken by smallest index, matching the original's seed iteration and pruning behavior.\n\nThe upper bound at any point is members.size() + active.size(), since active only shrinks over time and each step adds one member. So if that bound falls below globalBest, I can safely abort that branch—but if it merely equals globalBest, it could still tie without replacing, so I shouldn't prune in that equal case.\n\nTie-breaking favors the smaller index, so I only prune when ub is strictly less than globalBest, keeping the result deterministic. I can track the shared best using a relaxed atomic read—since best_card only increases monotonically, a stale read is just a lower bound on the true value, so pruning decisions based on it remain safe. Aborted branches never matter since their true cardinality is provably below the eventual winner.\n\nNow I'm working out per-thread local best tracking and merging it into the global atomic via a compare-and-swap max loop, plus handling the outer round structure where clustered points get removed from the unclustered set each pass. I need to check what N the benchmark actually uses by default before deciding how aggressive to make the parallel scheduling, since pruning causes uneven per-seed cost and dynamic scheduling with a small chunk size seems like the right call here.\n\nSeed-level parallelism across the N candidate seeds per round is the real scalable axis, since later rounds naturally have fewer unclustered points and cheaper work. For validation, I'm planning to parallelize the per-cluster diameter computation into a vector computed concurrently, then keep the printing loop sequential to preserve output order, while leaving the synthetic data generation sequential since it's RNG-dependent and must stay deterministic.\n\nI'm deciding to unconditionally require OpenMP rather than guard it behind ifdefs — using find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED) and linking against OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX, with thread-local state inside a parallel region and dynamic scheduling for the distance loop, merged via critical sections. I'm also weighing whether -march=native could alter floating-point results through FMA contraction of the distance computation, since that affects whether outputs stay bit-identical to the original.\n\nI conclude distance symmetry holds exactly in IEEE arithmetic since the squared differences are equal regardless of subtraction order, so I can keep candidate-then-member ordering as in the original. Now I'm sketching out the per-seed initialization cost: computing max distance from each seed to all active points is O(N) per seed, so roughly N² per round.\n\nFor small N (1000) this is cheap, but for very large N a spatial grid restricted to the threshold radius could massively reduce the candidate set — though that adds complexity and determinism concerns around sorting neighbor indices. I'll defer that optimization and focus on active-set pruning plus seed-level parallelism for now, since N=1000 doesn't need it.\n\nMy plan is to first benchmark the original implementation at N=1000 and N=2000 with threshold 2.0, saving a copy for comparison before making changes.\n\n","time":{"start":1793022050281,"end":1793022083496},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793022215153,"sessionID":"ses_e878ee6f8ffeQv4kFbLWpQ48Ca","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"edit","callID":"toolu_01TawHvuGdFa5A7TA7p4mtkr","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/qtclustering_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_omp_r3/qtclustering/qtclustering.cpp","oldString":"// Find the closest unclustered point to the current cluster that maintains diameter < threshold\n// Returns -1 if no such point exists\nint findClosestPoint(const std::vector<int>& cluster_members,\n                     const std::vector<bool>& clustered,\n                     const std::vector<bool>& in_cluster,\n                     const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                     const double threshold,\n                     const int point_count) {\n    int closest_point = -1;\n    double min_diameter = std::numeric_limits<double>::max();\n    \n    // Try each unclustered point as a candidate\n    for (int candidate = 0; candidate < point_count; ++candidate) {\n        // Skip if already clustered or already in this cluster\n        if (clustered[candidate] || in_cluster[candidate]) continue;\n        \n        // Calculate the maximum distance from candidate to all cluster members\n        double max_dist = 0.0;\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < cluster_members.size(); ++i) {\n            const int member = cluster_members[i];\n            const double dist = distance(points[candidate], points[member]);\n            max_dist = std::max(max_dist, dist);\n        }\n        \n        // If adding this point keeps diameter below threshold and is better than current best\n        if (max_dist < threshold && max_dist < min_diameter) {\n            min_diameter = max_dist;\n            closest_point = candidate;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return closest_point;\n}\n\n// Generate a candidate cluster starting from a seed point\n// Returns the cardinality (size) of the cluster\nint generateCandidateCluster(const int seed_point,\n                              const std::vector<bool>& clustered,\n                              const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                              const double threshold,\n                              const int point_count,\n                              std::vector<int>* cluster_members = nullptr) {\n    std::vector<bool> in_cluster(point_count, false);\n    std::vector<int> members;\n    \n    // Add seed point\n    in_cluster[seed_point] = true;\n    members.push_back(seed_point);\n    \n    // Iteratively add closest points\n    while (static_cast<int>(members.size()) < point_count) {\n        // Find closest point to current cluster that maintains diameter < threshold\n        const int closest = findClosestPoint(members, clustered, in_cluster, points, \n                                             threshold, point_count);\n        \n        if (closest < 0) break; // No more points can be added\n        \n        in_cluster[closest] = true;\n        members.push_back(closest);\n    }\n    \n    // Copy members if requested\n    if (cluster_members) {\n        *cluster_members = members;\n    }\n    \n    return static_cast<int>(members.size());\n}","newString":"// Per-thread scratch space reused across seed points\nstruct Workspace {\n    std::vector<double> max_dist;  // max distance from each point to the cluster so far\n    std::vector<int> active;       // candidates still eligible, in ascending index order\n\n    explicit Workspace(const int point_count)\n        : max_dist(point_count, 0.0) {\n        active.reserve(point_count);\n    }\n};\n\n// Generate a candidate cluster starting from a seed point.\n//\n// Equivalent to repeatedly adding the unclustered point whose maximum distance\n// to the current members is smallest (ties -> lowest index) while that maximum\n// distance stays below the threshold.\n//\n// The maximum distance of a candidate to the cluster is non-decreasing as\n// members are added, so it is maintained incrementally, and candidates that\n// reach the threshold are dropped permanently.\n//\n// Pruning: the final cardinality is at most members + active candidates. If\n// that bound is strictly below a cardinality already achieved by some other\n// seed (best_known), this candidate can never win, so growth stops early and\n// -1 is returned.\n//\n// On return, `members` holds the cluster in insertion order.\nint generateCandidateCluster(const int seed_point,\n                             const std::vector<bool>& clustered,\n                             const std::vector<Point>& points,\n                             const double threshold,\n                             const int point_count,\n                             const std::atomic<int>& best_known,\n                             Workspace& ws,\n                             std::vector<int>& members) {\n    std::vector<double>& max_dist = ws.max_dist;\n    std::vector<int>& active = ws.active;\n\n    members.clear();\n    members.push_back(seed_point);\n    active.clear();\n\n    // Initial candidates: unclustered points within threshold of the seed\n    const Point& seed = points[seed_point];\n    for (int c = 0; c < point_count; ++c) {\n        if (clustered[c] || c == seed_point) continue;\n        const double d = distance(points[c], seed);\n        if (d < threshold) {\n            max_dist[c] = d;\n            active.push_back(c);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Select the candidate with smallest max distance (first index on ties)\n    int next = -1;\n    double next_d = std::numeric_limits<double>::max();\n    for (const int c : active) {\n        if (max_dist[c] < next_d) {\n            next_d = max_dist[c];\n            next = c;\n        }\n    }\n\n    while (next >= 0) {\n        if (static_cast<int>(members.size() + active.size()) <\n            best_known.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) {\n            return -1;
